overall: Atlanta's June 23rd high temperature day is effectively over, with the peak of 73.9°F recorded at 17:52 ET (~4.3 hours ago). The day was dramatically cooler than the NWS forecast of 86°F, driven by persistent overcast skies (OVC) through the morning hours and 0.74 inches of cumulative precipitation that caused a pronounced midday cool-down, with temperatures dipping to 66.2°F around 13:52-14:52 ET before recovering. Current temperature is 71.6°F and falling with zero velocity, confirming the daily max is locked in.
forecast_obs_notes: There is extreme divergence between NWP models and reality: HRRR (73.5°F) and ECMWF (74.2°F) were well-calibrated and closely bracketed the observed 73.9°F max, while NBM (79.5°F) and especially the NWS narrative forecast (86°F) were significant over-estimates — likely failing to fully account for the cloud/precipitation suppression that materialized. The intraday model correctly converged to 94.6% confidence in the 72–73°F bucket, consistent with the 73.9°F observed max.
max_temp_prediction: With 22:10 ET as the observation time, temperatures are cooling into the low 70s and will not rebound overnight. The running max of 73.9°F is the de facto final TMAX for June 23rd with near-certainty — the intraday model's 94.6% probability on the 72–73°F bucket (which captures 73.9°F) reflects this. Confidence is very high (>95%) that today's official TMAX will be reported as 73.9°F or within rounding to 74°F.
